transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Vectorly ML), Emily Chen (Vectorly Infra), Sanjay Rao (Vectorly Product)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off 
quick agenda: go through the INT8 results, FP8 notes, any regressions, then next steps. Sofia you good to start with the results?
[00:28] Sofia: Yeah totally. I'll share my screen in a sec but TL;DR, INT8 across our benchmark gives roughly 1.9 to 2.6x token/sec improvements depending on sequence length and batch. Latency p50 improves about 35-50% for 512 tokens, p95 20-30% depending on cold starts. We did see quality diffs on NER-style prompts, particularly entity hallucinations on person names.
[00:56] Raj: Can you unpack the hallucination bit? Are we seeing changed logits or more repetition?
[01:10] Sofia: It's more like the top-k shifts for low prob tokens. In a few cases FP16 returns the correct entity but INT8 returns a different name, so it's a precision quantization side effect around rarely seen tokens. Not huge for general QA prompts, but for named-entity extraction it's noticeable.
[01:36] Sanjay: Is that consistent across seeds? Or a fluke?
[01:42] Sofia: We ran 5 seeds; it reproduced on 3. So it's not just noise. We flagged the cases and added them to the eval set.
[02:05] Emily: Were these single-turn inferences or multi-turn chat? Because our system is mostly multi-turn and uses KV cache heavily.
[02:18] Sofia: Good point. Most of the initial runs were single-turn. We did a smaller multi-turn pass 
when KV cache is used, INT8 perf benefits remain but the delta in quality vs FP16 shrinks slightly, interestingly. Possibly because cache reduces the token distribution variance.
[02:45] Raj: Can you remind me of the hardware we ran on for these numbers?
[02:50] Sofia: Sure 
these were on g5.48x-ish nodes we had in the bench lab, the config is in the spreadsheet link I posted in the chat, but basically A100-ish equivalent; for FP8 we used a patched runtime with mixed kernels 
that's why FP8 numbers are more variable.
[03:12] Raj: You said FP8 numbers more variable 
what's the ballpark?
[03:20] Sofia: FP8 throughput is better than FP16 but not as stable as INT8 yet 
p50 gains around 1.4-1.8x vs FP16, p95 jitter higher, and we saw a few kernel falls back to slower path which spiked latency. That's a runtime stability issue, not fundamental model quality.
[03:44] Liam: Just to clarify for the team: INT8 today is the most mature quantization path for the runtime, FP8 is experimental with promising perf but some kernel maturity gaps.
[03:56] Raj: Do we have any numbers on end-to-end latency including network and marshalling? The numbers you gave sound like server-side perf only.
[04:06] Sofia: Good call. Those are server-side. We ran a couple of e2e tests through your current API gateway 
added ~15-25ms overhead. We'll do a full 2k sample e2e sweep per the action item.
[04:24] Emily: For the e2e runs can you replicate our VPC egress/ingress? We had issues with peering that changed latency last week.
[04:33] Sofia: Yes we'll set up bench nodes in your VPC once we have the allowlist and peering details. Emily, can you share the firewall rules?
[04:41] Emily: I'll drop them in the shared folder by EOD.
[04:44] Sanjay: Back to quality 
Raj, how painful are those NER regressions? Could we live with a small drop if throughput halves cost?
[04:55] Raj: For most of our UX it's okay; but for the entity extraction pipeline that feeds downstream billing it's sensitive. Even a 2-3% entity misclass rate triggers manual review workflows and adds ops cost.
[05:10] Sofia: One mitigation we discussed is selective precision 
keep FP16 for the NER model or the final answer reranker and serve the rest quantized. We tested a hybrid flow 
small perf hit but preserves critical accuracy.
[05:28] Liam: That's a common pattern 
route sensitive routes to higher precision, bulk generation to INT8. We can also set up automatic fallbacks based on a confidence threshold.
[05:38] Raj: How intrusive is the hybrid setup to our stack? We use the Redwood API; can we pin endpoints per route?
[05:47] Liam: Yep 
you can pin model versions per route in the config. You can have route-A point to FP16 model instance, route-B to INT8. The console can do it, or via API.
[05:58] Emily: Any security or audit differences between configs? We need audit logs for FP16 and INT8 ops separately.
[06:07] Sofia: We ingest token-level cost and trace per model variant; everything is logged and can be exported to your SIEM. It's the same audit paths, just different model tags.
[06:20] Sanjay: FP8 
what would the timeline look like to make it safe for prod?
[06:26] Sofia: If we commit engineering cycles, 4-6 weeks to stable kernels and careful regression testing. Meanwhile INT8 is safe for pilot.
[06:35] Raj: Did you run the evals on our production prompt set?
[06:40] Sofia: We ran on the 150 prompt subset you provided and added the NER failcases. The full 2k set hasn't been run end-to-end yet. That's part of next steps.
[06:52] Liam: Ok let's go into the spreadsheet 
I won't read everything but key rows: INT8 throughput averages, FP8 experimental, quality delta columns 
Raj flagged 6 prompts with >4% drop.
[07:10] Raj: Yep those 6 include a few with long tails (rare drug names, customer surnames).
[07:18] Emily: Could we apply prompt engineering or post-processing to fix these? Like entity canonicalization?
[07:25] Raj: We could, but that adds complexity. Prefer to solve at model serving level if possible.
[07:32] Sofia: Another lever is quant-aware calibration 
per-layer scale adjustments reduced some of the hallucinations in our internal tests. We can attempt a re-calibration on your specific checkpoints.
[07:46] Sanjay: Any cost math to share? If INT8 drops tokens/second cost by 2x, what's the delta in monthly run cost?
[07:54] Liam: We'll send a pricing example 
ballpark, raw GPU cost goes down ~40-60% depending on throughput improvements and effective concurrency. There's also software ops overhead change. I'll attach a sample deck after the call.
[08:08] Emily: For the bench nodes, do you need ephemeral keys or do you use our KMS?
[08:13] Sofia: For the bench we can use temp keys; for production we recommend integrating with your KMS/HSM 
we support CMKs and audit logs.
[08:22] Raj: Quick question: does INT8 affect embedding quality if we use same model for embeddings?
[08:29] Sofia: We didn't test embeddings in this run. Preliminary internal checks show embeddings degrade more for quantized models, so we usually keep embeddings in FP16/FP32 or use a separate float-only path. We can run a quick embedding quality check on your vectors if you want.
[08:44] Sanjay: Yes please add that to the run list.
[08:48] Sofia: Added.
[08:50] Liam: Any blockers from a sales/contract perspective? Are you leaning toward Dedicated reserve or hosted pilot?
[08:58] Sanjay: We're leaning toward a small Dedicated pilot for predictable throughput and to run these benchmarks in our VPC. But need pricing.
[09:07] Liam: Okay I'll send the Dedicated pilot pricing and an SOW template.
[09:11] Emily: We'll need the contract to include SOC2/ISO language 
legal will push.
[09:16] Liam: We have SOC 2 Type II docs and can add the ISO attestation; I'll include links.
[09:21] Raj: On the technical side, two asks: 1) end-to-end INT8 sweep 2k requests, run multi-turn KV cache tests, and 2) FP8 stability runs on same hardware to capture kernel fallbacks.
[09:36] Sofia: Confirmed. I'll run INT8 e2e 2k and multi-turn KV pass. For FP8 I'll capture kernel fallback logs and we can triage.
[09:46] Raj: What about monitoring/alerts? If we deploy INT8 at scale how do we detect a regression in real time?
[09:53] Sofia: We recommend a small canary set of prompts with automated evals and a regression alert tied to a quality delta threshold. We can configure that in Redwood Optimize and wire alerts to Slack or PagerDuty.
[10:07] Sanjay: That'd be great 
make sure it's per-route and per-model-variant so ops know where to roll back.
[10:15] Liam: We'll provide a Canary template.
[10:18] Emily: For the bench nodes we need to sync on network egress IPs so we can update firewall.
[10:24] Emily: (cont) I'll upload the CIDR and peering instructions.
[10:27] Liam: Thanks. Any other questions?
[10:30] Raj: One last: regression triage ownership 
if we find a failcase do we open a Redwood bug or coordinate through our SE?
[10:36] Sofia: Open a ticket to our SE portal and cc me; we'll prioritize POC regressions.
[10:42] Sanjay: Cool.
[10:44] Liam: Quick recap of action items, everyone: Sofia run INT8 e2e 2k + multi-turn KV by 7/20; Raj validate FP8/FP16 on 4 production prompts and add failures by 7/19; Emily share VPC/firewall/peering details by 7/18; Liam send Dedicated pricing and SOC2/ISO links by 7/16.
[11:05] Sanjay: Sounds good, thanks all.
[11:08] Liam: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and update the spreadsheet. Bye.
[11:12] (call ends)
